title: Growing French beans
subtitle: Dwarf and climbing varieties from sowing to picking
excerpt: French beans are sown outdoors after the last frost in May or June and cropped from July to October. Dwarf varieties need no support; climbing varieties reach 2 metres and produce over a longer period. Both need warmth to establish and regular picking to keep producing.
sourceNotes: RHS French bean growing guide (rhs.org.uk). USDA agricultural extension notes on snap bean production, public domain. Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), kitchen garden section.

glossaryTerms.definition: The point at which the seeds inside a French bean pod are visibly swollen but not yet fully ripe and dry. Beans left to the haricot stage are shelled and cooked fresh; dried haricot beans (used in cassoulet and baked beans) are left to ripen fully and dry on the plant before shelling.

content.text: French beans are quicker and less demanding than runner beans, with no need for tall canes unless you are growing a climbing variety. Dwarf varieties (Tendergreen, The Prince, Safari) form a compact bush and produce a concentrated crop over four to six weeks. Climbing varieties (Cobra, Fasold) require a cane or net support but crop over a longer period.

Full sun, well-drained, fertile soil. French beans are more cold-sensitive than peas and cannot be planted out until night temperatures are reliably above 10°C; late May in the south, early June in the north. Sow early indoors in 9 cm pots in late April for an earlier outdoor crop, or sow direct outdoors from late May.

Direct sow 5 cm deep, 8 to 10 cm apart in rows 45 cm apart. For a continuous supply, sow every three weeks from late May to mid-July. Germination takes 7 to 14 days in warm soil; below 10°C the seeds rot before germinating. For module sowing, one seed per cell, transplant at two to three weeks old without disturbing the roots.

French beans fix their own nitrogen in root nodules, so additional feeding is not usually needed in reasonable soil. Water at the base; wetting the foliage encourages fungal problems. In dry weather, water heavily at the base every three to four days. Climbing varieties need support from planting; put canes or a net in place before the plants need it.
Pick when the pods snap cleanly and before the beans inside are visible as bumps. At the
the pods become stringy and the plant slows production. Pick every two days at peak season. For dried haricot beans, leave a proportion of pods to ripen fully on the plant and harvest once brown.

items.symptom: Seeds fail to germinate, or germinate then collapse
items.cause: Soil too cold or too wet at sowing time.
items.fix: Wait until the soil temperature reaches at least 12°C. Pre-germinate seeds on damp kitchen paper indoors before sowing, or sow into 9 cm pots on a windowsill and plant out once rooted.
Remove affected leaves. Improve air circulation by thinning. Rust rarely kills healthy plants; crop quality is unaffected if plants are otherwise well grown.
